record.paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of analytic multifunctions
record.context_brief: open mapping theorem; boundary of range
record.original_question: Let D be a plane domain, and let K be an analytic multifunction on D whose values K(z) are polynomially convex for every z in D. Is it always true that every point of K(D) lying outside the interior of K(D) belongs to every fiber K(z)? Equivalently, must K(D) \ int(K(D)) be contained in the intersection of the sets K(z) over all z in D?

evidence.quote: This example and other similar ones strongly suggest that non-interior points of K(D) should be permanently in K(z), in other words, that K(D) \ int(K(D)) subseteq intersection over z in D of K(z).
Problem B. Let K be an analytic multifunction on a domain D whose values K(z) are polynomially convex sets. Must (3) hold?
The general case is still an open problem (no pun intended!).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be a domain in the complex plane. An analytic multifunction $K$ on $D$ is a map assigning to each $z \in D$ a non-empty compact subset $K(z) \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ such that the graph $\{(z,w) \in D \times \mathbb{C} : w \in K(z)\}$ is closed and the complement $(D \times \mathbb{C}) \setminus \mathrm{graph}(K)$ is pseudoconvex (equivalently, $z \mapsto \log\,\mathrm{dist}(w, K(z))$ is superharmonic for every fixed $w \in \mathbb{C}$, after the standard adjustments). A compact set $L \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ is polynomially convex if it equals its polynomial hull $\widehat{L} = \{w \in \mathbb{C} : |p(w)| \le \max_{L} |p| \text{ for every polynomial } p\}$.

Set $K(D) = \bigcup_{z \in D} K(z)$ and let $\mathrm{int}(K(D))$ denote its topological interior in $\mathbb{C}$.

Question. Suppose that $K$ is an analytic multifunction on $D$ such that $K(z)$ is polynomially convex for every $z \in D$. Must every point of $K(D)$ that does not lie in $\mathrm{int}(K(D))$ belong to $K(z)$ for every $z \in D$? Equivalently, does the inclusion
$$K(D) \setminus \mathrm{int}(K(D)) \;\subseteq\; \bigcap_{z \in D} K(z)$$
always hold?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a known open problem in the theory of analytic multifunctions, associated with open mapping-type theorems for polynomially convex valued analytic multifunctions. Special cases (e.g., convex-valued or polar-valued multifunctions) have been settled affirmatively, but the general case appears to remain unresolved according to available references on analytic multifunctions and polynomial convexity.

status_evidence.title: Two new open mapping theorems for analytic multifunctions
status_evidence.snippet: Open mapping theorems for analytic multifunctions, with results in special cases such as convex-valued and polar-valued multifunctions.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is established in special cases (convex-valued, polar-valued), but the general statement is not proved.

status_evidence.title: Polynomial convexity - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Background on polynomial convexity and analytic structure of polynomial hulls; several related questions remain open.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related questions on polynomial hulls and analytic structure remain unresolved in general.
